stemMd: Which statement correctly distinguishes cholesterol from a triglyceride?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Triglycerides contain only phosphate groups and no carbon.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Both consist of three amino-acid chains.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Cholesterol has a fused-ring carbon skeleton; a triglyceride contains glycerol esterified to three fatty acids.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Cholesterol is the universal monomer of DNA.

explanationMd: A triglyceride is a triester used in energy storage. Cholesterol is a steroid with a fused-ring framework. Recognising the structural families avoids treating all lipids as the same molecule.

distractorRationale.e: Their structures and cellular roles differ.
